clue.text: Enjoy the sunshine before monster film, dance and game

parts.note: to bask is to lie enjoying warmth and sun
E.T. is Spielberg's film about a small alien creature
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A day out: sunbathing, then a creature feature, then dancing and a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Basketball is a team sport played by shooting a ball through a hoop.

clue.text: Most austere bachelor needing a break

parts.note: a rest is a break from work

explanation.surface: A strict single man who badly needs time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Barest is the superlative of bare, meaning plainest or most stripped of ornament.

clue.text: Fish primarily served with fruit (after removal of tail)

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of the word served
the last letter of the fruit's name is cut off before it is used

parts.note: the almond is botanically the fruit of the almond tree

explanation.surface: A fish dish served with fruit, with a note on preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: The almond counts as a fruit botanically, though most solvers think of it as a nut; 'after removal of tail' clips its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The salmon is a large food fish that runs up rivers to spawn.

clue.text: One may leave the world behind at this rate

definitions.text: One may leave the world behind at this rate

parts.words: One may leave the world behind at this rate
parts.note: the surface suggests a dying person or escapist, but the rate meant is the speed a rocket needs to break free of Earth's gravity

explanation.definitionFit: This physics term is the minimum speed an object needs to break free of a planet's gravitational pull.

clue.text: Made mistake and lost blood having got trapped below

indicators.note: the word for below is held inside the word for lost blood

parts.note: to bleed is to lose blood, past tense bled
under means below

explanation.surface: Someone erred and bled after being pinned beneath something.
explanation.definitionFit: To blunder is to make a clumsy error.

clue.text: Take a walk to the north to find wild animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a mall is a sheltered public walk or promenade, as in Pall Mall

explanation.surface: Advice to stroll northwards in search of wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns A MALL upwards in the down light. A mall in its original sense is a tree-lined walk.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal related to the camel, here loosely called wild.

clue.text: Old American gets hold of piano work

indicators.note: the old American pair grip the letter for piano between them

parts.note: P is the musical marking for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: An elderly American takes possession of a piano piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical composition, a numbered piece of a composer's output.

clue.text: Bath water? They drink it here

definitions.text: Bath water? They drink it here

parts.words: Bath water? They drink it here
parts.note: Bath is the English spa city, not a tub, and its mineral water was drunk by visitors in a famous Georgian hall

explanation.walkthrough: The capital B is disguised at the start: Bath is the Somerset spa city, whose eighteenth-century hall served the spring water to visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A pump room is a hall at a spa where the medicinal spring water is dispensed for drinking.

clue.text: Susan entertains Europeans and Africans

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so one word holds the other

parts.note: Sue is a short form of Susan
Danes are people from Denmark

explanation.surface: A hostess named Susan has guests from Europe and Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Sudan, a country in north-east Africa, are Sudanese.

clue.text: Must-have object? Shalt get it then, somehow!

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of the four words are made to fit in some new way

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding command urging someone to acquire the coveted item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges SHALT GET IT THEN, fourteen letters, into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget everyone wants is described as the newest craze or fashion.

clue.text: You're licensed to house something old and valuable

indicators.note: the two words shelter the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A licence to keep an antique in your home.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a treasured object surviving from the past.

clue.text: Bold-faced girl, a maiden shut in hut

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: the A and the maiden letter are enclosed by the word for hut

parts.note: a shed is a simple hut
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A brazen girl locks a young woman inside a shack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut in' places A and M (a maiden over in cricket) inside SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold-faced means shameless or brazen, showing no embarrassment.

clue.text: Finished pre-eminent having rushed around

indicators.note: the word for rushed goes around the word for pre-eminent

parts.note: sped means hurried or rushed
top means best or pre-eminent

explanation.surface: A leading competitor, having hurried round the course, has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopped means ceased or came to an end.

clue.text: A loner, I get troubled and flap

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A solitary person admits to getting upset and panicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get troubled' rearranges A LONER I; the definition 'flap' is a noun, not panic.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged control surface on an aircraft wing.

clue.text: A curious vote, sadly going for the ultra-safe option?

indicators.note: sadly signals that the words are handled badly, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An odd election result where voters played it far too safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcautious describes someone excessively careful who always avoids risk.

clue.text: A garment little girl keeps on is repsonsible for scratches

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment

indicators.note: the little girl word holds the word on inside it

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a little girl in the family

explanation.surface: An item of clothing a young girl insists on wearing leaves marks on the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repsonsible' is a misspelling in the clue as held; 'is responsible for' just links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasions are scrapes or grazes where skin has been rubbed away.

clue.text: Get more excited about Euclid's introduction? One might!

definitions.text: Get more excited about Euclid's introduction? One might!

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the starting letter of the Greek mathematician's name
excited letters are stirred up and rearranged
introduction asks for the first letter of Euclid's

explanation.surface: A mathematician thrilled by Euclid's opening book would be this kind of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges GET MORE to GEOMTER, and 'about' wraps it round E from Euclid.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometer is a specialist in geometry, the subject Euclid founded.

clue.text: Useful chap many had upset over nothing initially

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the anagram sits above the next piece
upset letters are knocked over and rearranged
initially asks for the first letter of nothing

explanation.surface: A capable man distressed that so many had nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MANY HAD to HANDYMA, placed 'over' N.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman is a man skilled at odd jobs and repairs.

clue.text: Sides alarmed about information put on to computer

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Both teams panic about data being loaded onto a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: An email address is the identifying detail entered to send electronic mail.

clue.text: Secure a gun after start of fight

indicators.note: after places the following pieces later in the answer than the first letter
start of asks for the opening letter of the word fight

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Grab a weapon once the battle begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten is to fix firmly or make secure.

clue.text: Like a cat jumping over lake in agitation

indicators.note: the cat word leaps over and so surrounds the letter for lake

parts.note: a cat is furry

explanation.surface: A cat leaping over a lake in a state of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A flurry is a sudden burst of nervous excitement or commotion.

clue.text: Token display of manners shown by copper to maiden

parts.note: modi is the Latin plural of modus, a manner or way
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A policeman shows a young woman a gesture of politeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the element. MODI, plural of the Latin modus, is a crossword staple for manners or ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A small token amount of something, such as courtesy, is a modicum of it.

clue.text: Riotous fight — yours truly needs shelter

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Caught in a brawl, the speaker looks for cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused hand-to-hand scuffle.

clue.text: Venture out from land — clots are unwell

parts.note: blood that clots sets or congeals
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: Idiots on shore are feeling sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clots' reads as fools but is the verb: blood clots, or sets.
explanation.definitionFit: To set sail is to begin a voyage by sea.

clue.text: It's silly to omit all fruit

indicators.note: silly letters are made to behave foolishly, into a new order

explanation.surface: It would be foolish to leave out all the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a small husked fruit used in Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Bury's season? Forget the first week

indicators.note: the opening letter of the season word is dropped

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A question about the football calendar at Bury, a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town and football club near Manchester; here it is the verb, with 's for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave.

clue.text: Money makes one almost frisky

indicators.note: almost means the frisky word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: randy means lustful or frisky

explanation.surface: Cash makes a person feel nearly frisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The rand is the currency of South Africa.

clue.text: Wag involved with scene in new York gives info to the media

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the new-York pair

parts.note: Y is short for York

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A footballer's partner mixes with the New York scene and tips off the press.
explanation.walkthrough: A WAG, short for 'wives and girlfriends', is a footballer's partner in British tabloid slang; 'in' puts the anagram between the New York letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A news agency is an organisation that gathers reports and supplies them to newspapers and broadcasters.
